7.1: With mind attached to Me and practising yoga in My refuge, you shall know Me fully — hear how.
7.2: I will teach you knowledge together with realisation, knowing which nothing more remains to be known.
7.3: Among thousands, scarcely one strives for perfection; among those who succeed, scarcely one knows Me in truth.
7.4: My lower nature is eightfold: earth, water, fire, air, ether, mind, intellect and ego.
7.5: That is the lower; know My higher nature to be the life-element by which this universe is sustained.
7.6: All beings have their birth in these two; I am the origin and the dissolution of the whole universe.
7.7: There is nothing higher than Me; all this is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.
7.8: I am the taste in water, the light in moon and sun, the syllable Om, sound in ether, manhood in men.
7.9: I am the sweet fragrance in earth, the brilliance in fire, the life in all beings, the austerity in ascetics.
7.10: Know Me as the eternal seed of all beings, the intelligence of the intelligent, the splendour of the splendid.
7.11: I am the strength of the strong, free of desire and attachment, and desire not opposed to dharma.
7.12: All states of sattva, rajas and tamas are from Me; they are in Me, but I am not in them.
7.13: Deluded by these three qualities, the world does not know Me, who am above them and imperishable.
7.14: This divine illusion of Mine is hard to cross; those who take refuge in Me alone cross beyond it.
7.15: The evildoers, deluded and lowest of men, robbed of knowledge by illusion, do not seek Me.
7.16: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the wise.
7.17: Of these, the wise one, ever steadfast and devoted to the One, excels — I am dear to that one, and that one to Me.
7.18: All these are noble, but the wise one I regard as My very Self, established in Me as the highest goal.
7.19: At the end of many births, the wise take refuge in Me, seeing that all is Vasudeva — such a soul is very rare.
7.20: Those whose knowledge is carried away by desires resort to other gods, following their own natures.
7.21: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that faith of theirs steady.
7.22: Endowed with that faith, they worship and obtain their desires — but those desires are granted by Me alone.
7.23: The fruit gained by the small-minded is finite; worshippers of gods go to the gods, My devotees come to Me.
7.24: The unintelligent think I, the unmanifest, have taken form, not knowing My higher, imperishable nature.
7.25: Veiled by My yoga-illusion, I am not manifest to all; this deluded world does not know Me as unborn and imperishable.
7.26: I know all beings past, present and to come — but no one knows Me.
7.27: All beings fall into delusion at birth, deceived by the pairs of opposites arising from desire and aversion.
7.28: Those of virtuous deeds, whose sin has ended, freed from the delusion of the pairs, worship Me steadfastly.
7.29: Those who strive for freedom from age and death, taking refuge in Me, know Brahman entirely and the whole of action.
7.30: Those who know Me as the principle of being, of the gods and of sacrifice, know Me even at the hour of death.
